freebsd_15_aarch64.base_config: GENERIC (arm64 includes std.arm64 + platform SoC includes)
freebsd_15_aarch64.strategy: Use arm64 GENERIC, enable virtio, ENA, gve as modules; Xen not supported on arm64 in FreeBSD; Hyper-V VMBus not yet ported to arm64.
notes: XENHVM option only exists in options.amd64 and options.i386, NOT options.arm64 — Xen HVM guest is amd64-only in FreeBSD.
Hyper-V device (hv_vmbus) historically amd64-only in FreeBSD; Azure ARM64 VMs (Cobalt) may require Hyper-V arm64 support not yet upstream.
GCP ARM instances REQUIRE gve driver (gVNIC mandatory for ARM machine types).
Apple HVF/Hypervisor.framework: FreeBSD arm64 runs via UTM/QEMU with HVF acceleration; virtio is the device model.
AWS Graviton (aarch64) instances: ENA driver supports aarch64 since FreeBSD 13 (stable/12 from r345872).

devices.entry: device virtio + virtio_pci + vtnet + virtio_blk + virtio_scsi + virtio_balloon

devices.arch_note: GCP ARM VMs REQUIRE gVNIC — no vtnet fallback on newer GCP ARM machine types
devices.source: GCP docs: ARM CPU platform must use gVNIC

freebsd_15_aarch64.xen_status: NOT SUPPORTED on FreeBSD aarch64 — XENHVM option absent from options.arm64
freebsd_15_aarch64.hyperv_status: NOT PORTED to FreeBSD aarch64 — Azure Cobalt (ARM64) requires investigation; Azure may provide virtio fallback
freebsd_15_aarch64.vmware_status: VMware ARM (Apple Silicon host) uses virtio; pvscsi/vmx not needed

notes: FreeBSD 15 retains ARMv7 as Tier 2 (armv7 = ARMv7-A hard-float).
FreeBSD 16 will drop ARMv7 per Feb 2024 announcement.
No cloud provider offers ARMv7 instances; physical hardware only (Pi 2, older ARM boards).
virtio works on ARMv7 via virtio_mmio for QEMU; PCI virtio also works if board has PCIe.

32-bit binary compat on amd64 (COMPAT_FREEBSD32) is retained.

NetBSD 11.0 introduces MICROVM kernel for extremely fast PVH/virtio-MMIO boot.
Standard virtio drivers: ld(4) [block], vioif(4) [net], vioscsi(4) [scsi], viomb(4) [balloon], viornd(4) [rng], viocon(4) [console].
NetBSD lacks native cloud-init; see cloud-init-strategy.md for alternatives.
Xen: NetBSD has Xen port (XEN3 kernel); dom0 and domU supported on amd64.
Hyper-V: No native Hyper-V drivers in NetBSD 11 mainline — QEMU emulation only.
VMware: No native VMXNET3/PVSCSI in NetBSD — use E1000 emulation.

firecracker.bsd_support: NOT SUPPORTED — Firecracker officially supports Linux and OSv only; no BSD guest support documented. Boot path (direct vmlinux load, no EFI) is incompatible with BSD loaders.
firecracker.kata_containers: Kata wraps Firecracker or QEMU; same constraints apply

cloud_hypervisor.bsd_support: Officially supports Linux + Windows; FreeBSD POSSIBLE with virtio drivers but not documented as supported
cloud_hypervisor.boot: PVH for x86 or direct kernel; UEFI OVMF supported

required_guest_drivers: virtio-* for performance; falls back to emulated hardware (RTL8139, ISA, etc.)
qemu_tcg.notes: Slowest option but supports every architecture combination

gvisor.explanation: gVisor intercepts syscalls at the application level using a userspace kernel (Sentry). It does not present a hypervisor interface to guest OS kernels. genoa images cannot 'run on' gVisor — gVisor runs containers, not VMs. The Sentry IS the kernel; there is no guest kernel slot.
gvisor.architecture: amd64 only for the sandbox; x86_64 Linux host required

wsl2.explanation: WSL2 runs a Microsoft-provided Linux kernel in a Hyper-V VM. Custom kernels are possible (specify in .wslconfig) but must be Linux kernels. BSD images cannot run in WSL2. Document as out-of-scope for genoa.

arch_support: aarch64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5, Ampere servers, AWS Graviton hardware)
bare_metal.notes: Bare metal requires actual device drivers beyond virtio; cloud/VM kernel image insufficient without board-specific drivers
